caption:
Resolution tells you what something is. Cadence tells you when it changed. For warning problems, cadence is the one that matters.

A sharp image taken once a month can miss a flood crest, a new access road, or a tank farm filling up — because the change happened in the gap, not on the day of the pass. A coarser image taken every few days catches the same event while it is still forming.

The Numan flood hindcast in September 2022 made this case directly. The reach-monitoring array flagged the rising-water signature four days ahead of the official warning — not because the imagery was exceptionally detailed, but because the site was being looked at often enough to see the trend before it became the crisis.

Buying detail without buying frequency is a common mistake. Know which one the problem actually needs before tasking either.
